ca_hall_of_horrors.blurb: Hall of Horrors is a group of rock formations in Joshua Tree National Park, on the northwest side of Park Boulevard across from Saddle Rocks. The rocks stand in parallel lines that form the halls of the name. Trad is the main event, with a good number of sport routes and top-ropes and a few boulder problems. The climbs run from moderate cracks to difficult sport lines and runout slabs, from about 5.5 to 5.12, with the most routes at 5.10 and a good spread of moderates from 5.7 to 5.9. There is little shade here, so the cooler months are the better bet. The biggest walls are East Wall Inner (Exorcist Area), South Horror Rock and West Wall Inner (Jane's Addiction Area), with North Horror Rock beside them.

ca_lion_s_den_menifee.blurb: The Lion's Den is a hilly bouldering area near Menifee, in California's Inland Empire, with sandy ground and chaparral and open grassland along the approach. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V4, a handful harder, and a few top-rope lines and one sport slab on the side. The Lion's Den itself holds the most climbs, followed by Serengeti and Ramona Egg Ranch Boulders. Mild winters, roughly December through March, are described as ideal, while summers run hot and call for early mornings or late afternoons. The south-facing rock catches a lot of sun, though the hillier sections and the larger boulders offer some shade.

ca_mount_shasta_area.blurb: The Mount Shasta Area covers the town of Mount Shasta in northeast California and the volcano that gives it its name. Away from the peak, the climbing is mostly small crags and bouldering areas in and near town. Bouldering is the biggest share, from V0 to about V6, followed by sport routes, mostly 5.9 to 5.12, and a smaller amount of trad. The mountain itself adds a few ice, alpine and mountaineering routes; Mount Shasta and Shastina have many summit routes, but no trails lead to the top, so climbers follow routes. South Fork holds the most climbs, with Sand Flat Boulders, Cantara Loop and The Dungeon among the other main spots.

co_lookout_mountain_road.blurb: A string of crags lines Lookout Mountain Road as it climbs west out of Golden, Colorado. The rock is mostly granite and gneiss, with occasional schist. Trad leads, with a solid share of sport, plus top-ropes, a few boulder problems and a small dry-tooling area for mixed climbs. Grades run from about 5.3 to 5.12, with most routes between 5.5 and 5.10 and the heaviest numbers at 5.7 to 5.9. Tiers of Zion holds the most climbs, on the northwest face of Mount Zion, with both single-pitch and multipitch routes. Lookout Mountain Crag, Lover's Leap on Beaver Brook and Crimson Tide Wall add more. Lookout Mountain Crag and Tiers of Zion are both described as shaded.

il_ferne_clyffe_cedar_bluff.blurb: Ferne Clyffe and Cedar Bluff sit in southern Illinois around Goreville, about two hours from St. Louis. The main climbing is at Ferne Clyffe State Park, a forested park with sandstone bluffs, and Cedar Bluff is a second, satellite area. Bolted single-pitch sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a good number of top-rope lines and a few trad lines and boulder problems. Grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.12, with a thinner set of moderates from 5.4 to 5.9 and a few routes reaching 5.13 and 5.14. The stone suits moderate climbers moving from the gym to outdoor sport climbing.
